brief: GS desk notes on power trade flows. Headwinds (midterms, rates, diesel, OEM overcapacity, lack of incremental BTM data-center contracts, PJM/ERCOT reforms, NIMBY) are weighed against tailwinds (resilient hyperscaler capex, PJM power price moves, bullish BTM previews, general power tightness), giving a playbook of muted deal announcements near term into midterms, then acceleration post-November into year end. On IPPs, the pushback that existing capacity would not land hyperscaler contracts has been dropped in the last 48 hours and specialists are warming; the PJM-vs-ERCOT trade is debated as middle vs later innings. BTM specialist positioning has eased to roughly 8/10 from near 10/10 in late summer but desks still expect more deal announcements (AESI, PUMP, SEI already positive; LBRT targeting 500MW by year end; WMB a possible announcement at earnings or by year end); financing is not expected to change, and Tier 1 vs Tier 2 operator distinctions are a live focus. Nuclear has been pressured for months, but CEG's 890MW uprate signals hyperscaler demand for baseload power; construction and cost risk still keep others from FIDs, and the uranium read-through from uprates should be positive.
